title: Grandfather's sweet potatoes and healthier food
summary: Digging sweet potatoes and baking them in ashes; thinks the old diet was healthier; hints at a coming hit record.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did y'all have any, since you're out in the rural areas, did y'all have any, did we grow any vegetables, have a garden, or did anybody?

Yeah, well, my grandfather, well, we didn't, I didn't have any, we didn't have any room to grow any vegetables, but my grandfather did plant, plant, in his yard there was a gentleman that had a big open field when we were living on Andover Street, right behind, he used to plant sweet potatoes. Cause I remember in the winter, we go, when he wasn't looking, we go out there and dig up some sweet potatoes and go home and wash them, and put them right in the ashes, in the, in the, in the, see cause of the fireplace, either the fireplace, which was buying the wood, or we used to go pick up coal on the, on the railroad, or the stove, just put the potatoes right down the mashes. And, uh, that's another meal. Yeah. Which I still say, you know, we ate sparingly, but I think the food was a little bit more healthier then. Yeah. Yeah. That's why I believe the older people today, the young people might get bigger, but I think we, maybe we'll, our body structure was a little different because I know from my body, but maybe I took care of myself. You know, I don't have to be no baron, but you know, I can say this, you know, I don't catch no cold. I don't get sick. And I'm 60 years old and I say, the good Lord been holding me for this hit record I got coming. I said, oh. Okay, we'll talk about that.
